clues.text: This city is hilly, which is rare in its flat southern state. It sits at the southern end of a red hills region.
clues.narrowing: Points to a hilly inland city in a famously flat state.

source.quote: Tallahassee's terrain is hilly by Florida standards, being at the southern end of the Red Hills Region, just above the Cody Scarp.

clues.text: Summers here are long and tropical, hotter than the beach towns to the south. Winters are short and mild, with barely a touch of cold.
clues.narrowing: Keeps inland southern capitals with long tropical summers.

source.quote: Tallahassee has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen: Cfa), with long, tropical summers and short, mild winters, as well as warm to hot, drier springs and autumns.

clues.text: The lawmakers were tired of long boat trips to two far ports. In 1824, they chose this old town site, halfway in between.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to the site two commissioners picked as a halfway point.

source.quote: Two appointed commissioners selected Tallahassee, then an Apalachee settlement (Anhaica) virtually abandoned after Andrew Jackson burned it in 1818, as a halfway point.

clues.text: This city's name is a Muskogean word. It is often translated as "old fields" or "old town".
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital's name means 'old fields' in Muskogean.

source.quote: The name Tallahassee is a Muskogean word often translated as "old fields" or "old town".

clues.text: The governor of Florida works in this city. The state capitol tower rises here, near the top of one of its high hills.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and lawmakers of Florida work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital city of the U.S. state of Florida

reveal.blurb: Two commissioners picked this halfway spot in 1824 so lawmakers would stop sailing between two distant old capitals. Its name is a Muskogean word meaning "old fields," and its hills surprise visitors in a flat state. The building is the capitol, and the city is the capital. Tallahassee is the capital of Florida.
